worked_solution:
We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}4x-\frac{\pi }{3} & =\frac{\pi }{3}+n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving our equation for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4x & =\frac{\pi }{3}+\frac{\pi }{3}+n\pi  \\ 4x & =\frac{2\pi }{3}+n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{\pi }{6}+\frac{n\pi }{4} \\ x & =\frac{(3n+2)\pi }{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x=\frac{\pi }{6}$

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x=\frac{5\pi }{12}$

- Setting $n=2$ gives $x=\frac{2\pi }{3}$

- Setting $n=3$ gives $x=\frac{11\pi }{12}$

- Setting $n=4$ gives $x=\frac{7\pi }{6}$

- Setting $n=5$ gives $x=\frac{17\pi }{12}$

- Setting $n=6$ gives $x=\frac{5\pi }{3}$

- Setting $n=7$ gives $x=\frac{23\pi }{12}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$ 

So, the solutions to the equation, in ascending order, are 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & =\frac{\pi }{6},\,{x}_{2}=\frac{5\pi }{12},\,{x}_{3}=\frac{2\pi }{3},\,{x}_{4}=\frac{11\pi }{12}, \\ {x}_{5} & =\frac{7\pi }{6},\,{x}_{6}=\frac{17\pi }{12},\,{x}_{7}=\frac{5\pi }{3},\,{x}_{8}=\frac{23\pi }{12}.\end{aligned}
$$
